title.narrative: Improve immediate access to food for Vulnerable drought affected HHS in, Barka, Towfiiq and Sinkaleer villages of Jamame districts with emergency multi purpose cash transfer (MPCA)

description.narrative: ltpgtJamame District is facing a severe food security crisis driven by consecutive droughts, erratic rainfall, flooding in 2025, insecurity, and persistently high food prices. According to the FSNAU IPC analysis for April–June 2025, Community engagement report of Dec-2025, more than 53% of the rural population is classified in IPC Phase 3 (Crisis) or above, with over 33,000 people experiencing acute food insecurity. These compounding shocks have significantly eroded household coping capacities, depleted productive assets, and increased protection risks, particularly for women, children, persons with disabilities, and minority groups. Women especially pregnant and lactating mothers are at heightened risk of malnutrition, while boys and girls are increasingly exposed to child labor, early marriage, and other harmful coping strategies. ltbrgtThe project aims to reduce vulnerability and combat severe food insecurity by improving immediate access to food for 605 vulnerable households, representing 3,630 people in IPC Phase 3 and above, through emergency Multi-Purpose Cash Assistance (MPCA) delivered in a protection-sensitive and community-led manner. The intervention will reach internally displaced persons and vulnerable host community members, with women comprising 55% of beneficiaries and children accounting for 65%. Approximately 363 persons with disabilities will be included. Priority will be given to female-headed households, families with malnourished children, pregnant and lactating women, persons with disabilities, elderly-headed households, and households that have lost assets due to drought or flooding.ltbrgtBy the end of the project, 605 households including 700 women, 260men, 910 boys, and 1760 girls are expected to demonstrate improved food consumption scores and reduced reliance on negative coping strategies. The intervention will contribute directly to Food Security Cluster objectives by ensuring dignified, equitable, and timely access to food through cash-based assistance, while also strengthening protection outcomes for women, girls, boys, and persons with disabilities. Himilo Organization for Development (HoD) will coordinate closely with the Food Security Cluster, OCHA, ABC structures, and local authorities to avoid duplication and ensure harmonized implementation. Risks related to access, security, and financial management will be mitigated through strong community acceptance, flexible planning, SHF-compliant systems, and regular monitoring. Overall, the project provides a timely, life-saving response to acute food insecurity in Jamame District by combining emergency cash assistance with strong protection measures, accountability, and community ownership to stabilize vulnerable households and prevent further deterioration of the humanitarian situation.ltbrgtTo achieve the stated objective and outcomes, HoD will undertake a series of integrated activities. These include training HoD staff on Sexual Exploitation and Abuse (SEA) prevention, organizational codes of conduct, safeguarding principles, accountability mechanisms, and survivor-centered approaches. HoD will also conduct 4 community mobilization meetings, beginning with consultations with local authorities as the primary entry point, followed by engagement with community members and prospective beneficiaries in Sinkaleer, Barka and Towfiiq villages of Jamame District. These meetings will facilitate the establishment of a Community Project Committee (CPC) comprising 15 members, with each village represented by five members, including two women and three men. In addition, HoD will conduct an intensive two-day training for CPC members and designated community SEA focal points to strengthen community-level prevention and response to SEA. Finally, HoD will register and select 605 households to receive three cycles of MPCA and will carry out four Post-Distribution Monitoring (PDM) exercises to assess cash utilization, effectiveness, and protection outcomeslt/pgtltpgtlt/pgt
